test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If a book is lying on a table and is not moving, which of the forces are balanced?

options.text: Weight of the book and normal reaction by the table
Weight of the book and friction
Only the weight of the book acts

solution:
The correct answer is __**Weight of the book and normal reaction by the table**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a book is lying stationary on a table, it is in a state of **static equilibrium**, meaning the **net force** acting on the object is **zero**.
 
• The **Weight of the book** is the **gravitational force** exerted by the **Earth** on the book, acting **vertically downwards** toward the center of the Earth.
 
• The **Normal reaction force** is the support force exerted by the **surface of the table** onto the book, acting **vertically upwards**, perpendicular to the surface.
 
• According to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, an object at rest stays at rest unless acted upon by an unbalanced force; since the book is not moving, the **upward normal force** must exactly **magnitude-wise** equal the **downward gravitational force**.
 
• These two forces are **balanced forces** because they act on the **same object** (the book), are equal in magnitude</st
